macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks surge after Democrats win control of Congress
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped about 3%, or roughly 1,500 points, while the S&P 500 gained about 1.6%-1.8% and the Nasdaq rose roughly 1.5%-2.1% after Democrats took control of both chambers of Congress. Investors interpreted the result as likely to produce divided government and policy checks, while solar stocks rallied and data-center and defense shares weakened.[1][3][6]

items.title: Oil prices plunge as markets reassess U.S. policy and Middle East risks
items.summary: U.S. crude fell 8.3% to $88.12 a barrel, extending its weekly decline to 15.4%, as investors anticipated a possible diplomatic shift involving Iran and reduced the probability of near-term military escalation. The energy sector fell sharply during the equity rally.[4][7]

items.title: Eurozone inflation rises to 4%
items.summary: Eurozone inflation reached 4% in October, driven by higher energy costs and standing at twice the European Central Bank’s target. The increase is adding pressure on policymakers and raising expectations that European interest rates may remain higher for longer.[1]

items.title: Fed policy remains a focus as markets weigh inflation risks
items.summary: Markets continued to assess the Federal Reserve’s rate path amid inflation concerns and higher energy prices. Treasury borrowing plans were unchanged for coming months, while investors monitored the prospect of tighter policy and reduced expectations for near-term rate cuts.[1][10]

items.title: AMD reports strong quarterly growth
items.summary: Advanced Micro Devices beat Wall Street expectations, with quarterly revenue of $13.38 billion, up 45% year over year. Its data-center business grew 97% to $8.55 billion, supporting renewed investor interest in AI-related semiconductor demand despite broader concerns about AI infrastructure spending.[2][10]

items.title: Block shares jump after earnings beat and outlook increase
items.summary: Block shares rose about 9% in premarket trading after the payments company reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings and raised its gross-profit outlook for the following year.[3]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $80,000 as Democrats take control of Congress
items.summary: Bitcoin rose 3.77% over 24 hours to $80,428 after briefly falling near $75,000 during U.S. midterm vote counting. Ether gained 6.36% to $2,423, while major altcoins also advanced.[1]

items.title: U.S. crypto market-structure legislation faces greater uncertainty
items.summary: Democratic control of both chambers of Congress is expected to complicate or delay the crypto-focused CLARITY Act. House Democrats are reportedly considering a broader market-structure bill that would strengthen the SEC’s role.[1][3]

items.title: Trump-linked crypto tokens fall after midterm results
items.summary: Official Trump fell 20.48% over 24 hours, while Official Melania Meme dropped 13.18% and World Liberty Financial declined 6.68% as markets reassessed the political outlook for the projects.[1]

items.title: Riot Platforms reports strong quarter and major AI data-center lease
items.summary: Riot mined 1,637 Bitcoin in the third quarter, up from 1,406 a year earlier, and announced a 15-year lease covering its Corsicana campus. The agreement is expected to generate approximately $28 billion in contracted revenue over its initial term.[4]

items.title: Binance theft investigation points to fake-recruitment attack
items.summary: A preliminary investigation reportedly found that attackers began with a fake recruitment operation, compromised an engineer’s device, and used internal access to steal deployment credentials. Binance said it had frozen or intercepted about $2.85 billion and compensated 98% of affected assets.[10]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Ricursive Intelligence releases Ripple-65B for chip design
items.summary: Ricursive Intelligence released Ripple-65B Preview, an open-weight general-purpose model developed for its AI chip-design platform. The company says it achieved a score of 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1, which it described as a U.S. open-weight state-of-the-art result for agentic coding.[1]

items.title: Tencent unveils Hy4 multimodal AI model
items.summary: Tencent announced Hy4, a 770-billion-parameter model with image understanding, computer-use capabilities, and support for long-duration agent tasks such as CAD and game development. Tencent said the model includes safeguards against cyber misuse and plans to release its weights and technical documentation soon.[4][9]

items.title: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor
items.summary: Meta acquired Conductor, a startup whose tools help developers manage multiple coding agents. The deal reflects intensifying competition among major AI companies to control developer workflows and enterprise coding adoption.[10]

items.title: OpenAI agrees to acquire Pierre Computer Company
items.summary: OpenAI announced an agreement to acquire Pierre Computer Company, developer of Code Storage and other open-source software-development tools. The companies will remain separate until the transaction closes and receives required approvals.[10]

items.title: Pangram Labs launches AI-image detection model
items.summary: Pangram Labs introduced Pangram Image 1.0, a model designed to detect AI-generated images. The company claims 99.2% detection and a 0.27% false-positive rate.[2]

items.title: Preferred Networks releases PLaMo 3 Translate
items.summary: Preferred Networks released the weights for PLaMo 3 Translate in four sizes ranging from 0.8 billion to 31 billion parameters. The translation-specialized model supports 53 languages and is designed to perform strongly on Japanese-English and multilingual Japanese translation.[2]

items.title: Meta researchers present GSLM2 speech model
items.summary: Meta researchers introduced GSLM2, a multi-stream speech model intended to learn linguistic structure directly from audio. Reported experiments used datasets of up to 6 million hours and models with up to 6.5 billion parameters.[2]

items.title: AI decision models gain momentum
items.summary: A growing category of decision-focused models is emphasizing classification accuracy, probability estimates, speed, and execution cost rather than text generation. Reports describe new offerings from TypeSafeAI, OpenAI, AWS, Microsoft, and Cloudflare.[7]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake releases on Switch 2
items.summary: Nintendo is releasing a full remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2 on November 5, coinciding with the series’ 40th anniversary. The remake reportedly includes upgraded visuals, voiced cutscenes, orchestral music, and revised controls.

items.title: GTA 6 reportedly reaches $751 million in digital preorders
items.summary: Sensor Tower estimates that Grand Theft Auto 6 has generated about $751 million from 7.71 million digital preorders on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The figures are unofficial, exclude physical sales, and come ahead of the game’s reported November 19 release.

items.title: The Elder Scrolls 6 reportedly remains more than two years away
items.summary: Following Bethesda’s reported announcement of the title Sentinel, Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier said The Elder Scrolls 6 is still more than two years from release. Bethesda has indicated that further details will not be shared soon.

items.title: God of War: Laufey delayed to May 2027
items.summary: Santa Monica Studio has reportedly delayed God of War: Laufey from mid-February to May 20, 2027. The studio said the additional time will be used to complete and polish the game.

items.title: Arkane workers blame Microsoft for studio closure
items.summary: Unionized Arkane workers said Microsoft’s hiring freeze contributed to delays and costs that were later cited as reasons for closing the studio. Ubisoft and other companies have reportedly expressed interest in acquiring Arkane Lyon, which is developing Marvel’s Blade.

items.title: Ubisoft reportedly among bidders for Arkane Lyon
items.summary: Ubisoft and at least two other gaming companies have reportedly made offers for Arkane Lyon. Microsoft is also said to be considering a management buyout, with a potential sale possibly allowing the studio to continue work on Marvel’s Blade.

items.title: Commodore C64 Ultimate expands into physical retail
items.summary: Commodore has signed an exclusive distribution deal to bring the C64 Ultimate to physical stores across parts of Europe, Africa, and Asia. A Cyberpunk 2077-themed version is also reportedly planned.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Qualcomm to supply equipment for SpaceX’s Starlink Mobile network
items.summary: Qualcomm said SpaceX selected it to provide radio equipment, baseband units and software for a planned nationwide Starlink Mobile terrestrial 5G network beginning in 2027. Qualcomm also reported strong automotive growth and expects non-phone businesses to offset slower smartphone dependence.
